patch_description: The current program relies only on a repulsion-style relaxation, which converges to configurations where the min distance is "locally pushed" but is not a true local optimum of the ratio dmin/dmax. A complementary, well-proven technique (used in the higher-scoring variants) is an annealed smooth surrogate: replace dmin and dmax by soft-min/soft-max over squared distances via logsumexp, and minimize that surrogate with L-BFGS while annealing tau to zero. This gradient-based method makes coordinated, simultaneous moves of all 14 points (unlike the greedy pairwise repulsion), and since the objective is built from squared distances it is smooth and well-conditioned for the optimizer. Adding this as a final polish stage applied to the best relaxed configuration, plus a few jittered polish restarts, should refine the ratio beyond what relaxation alone reaches, matching or beating the ~0.94 score of the best prior program while staying well within the time budget (the polish takes ~1s). The polish re-centers and re-normalizes (scale-invariant surrogate on d^2), so the returned points remain valid and normalized to unit diameter.
